title: Fine-Tuning
summary: Fine-tune only after prompting, retrieval and orchestration measurably fail, and prove with eval numbers that the tune pays for its data, training and serving.
outcome: Fine-tune only when cheaper options have run out, and show with evaluations that the tune was worth its total cost.

project.title: A LoRA That Beats a Prompted Baseline
deliverables: Pick a narrow, real task where the best prompt still fails measurably
Set the failure, success metric and passing threshold before training
Build the strongest prompted baseline (few-shot, retrieval where relevant) and score it on a held-out set
Create a clean, versioned dataset with leak-free train/validation/held-out splits
Run a reproducible SFT tune with LoRA or QLoRA from a shareable config; add preference tuning only if evals show a gap
Compare tuned vs prompted on the same held-out set: quality, latency, tokens and cost per 1k requests
Test off-task regressions and document at least one failure
Serve the adapter with the correct chat template and confirm it reproduces offline numbers
Write a one-page decision record with retraining triggers

modules.title: Should you fine-tune?

topics.d: Compared with prompts, retrieval, tools and stronger models.
Consistent style, unenforceable formats, narrow tasks, shorter prompts, small-model specialization.

topics.t: What it is not good for
topics.d: Changing facts (use retrieval) or undefined tasks.
A specific failure that persists after prompt and retrieval work.

topics.t: The full cost of a tune
topics.d: Data, training, evaluation, serving and retraining.
A new base model means redoing the work.

modules.tryIt: Take a task where a prompt struggles, spend an hour improving the prompt and adding examples, and record how much of the gap closes before any training.
modules.outcome: Decide whether a task justifies fine-tuning and name the failure, metric and ownership cost.
modules.mentalModel: Climb the ladder: prompt → retrieval → tools → stronger model → fine-tune, moving up only when the rung below has measurably failed.

modules.title: Data curation for fine-tuning

topics.d: Write the target behavior before collecting data.
Logs, expert demonstrations or filtered synthetic data, each with bias.
Template mismatches silently degrade the tune.
Mask loss so training targets assistant turns.
Hundreds of clean examples often beat thousands of noisy ones.
Duplicates, contradictions, wrong labels and truncation.
Mix common and hard cases.
Keep near-duplicates from crossing splits.
Screen for personal data and licensed material.
Dataset and config versioned together.

modules.tryIt: Write fifty examples by hand, generate fifty synthetically, then review all hundred and count how many you would keep.
modules.outcome: Produce a clean, versioned, correctly formatted dataset with a held-out test set.

modules.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)

topics.d: Nudges a model toward labeled examples by minimizing loss on targets.
Learning rate, epochs, batch size, sequence length and grad accumulation.
Updating all weights is rarely needed for narrow tasks.

topics.t: A first SFT run with TRL
topics.d: A small job where train and validation loss both fall.
Underfitting, overfitting and instability.
Gaining the narrow skill, losing general ability.
Lower loss does not guarantee better answers.
By validation behavior, not the last epoch.

modules.tryIt: Train on the same dataset for one, three and eight epochs, then compare validation curves and read ten outputs from each checkpoint.
modules.outcome: Run SFT, read its curves and pick a defensible checkpoint.
modules.mentalModel: Examples → loss on target tokens → small weight updates → checkpoint chosen on validation, not training loss.

modules.title: LoRA & QLoRA

topics.d: Freeze the base; train small low-rank matrices.
A 4-bit frozen base so the tune fits a smaller GPU.
Plus dropout, precision and quantization type.
Quality, memory, time and storage.
Rerunnable configs for open-weight tunes.
From params, precision, sequence length and batch size.
Dataset version, config and eval results per run.
Available bases and whether you keep the weights.

modules.tryIt: Run the same tune as LoRA at two ranks and as QLoRA, then compare peak GPU memory, training time, adapter size and held-out score.
modules.outcome: Fine-tune an open model efficiently on one GPU with reproducible results.
modules.mentalModel: Frozen base + small trained adapter = tuned behavior at a fraction of the memory and storage.

modules.title: Preference tuning & DPO

topics.d: One right answer vs 'A beats B'.
Chosen and rejected responses differing in the target quality.
Human raters, judges or feedback; measure agreement.
Pairs should not differ in irrelevant ways.
Raise likelihood of preferred over rejected answers without RL.
Preference tuning usually builds on an SFT checkpoint.
Tone, helpfulness, refusals and concision.
When preference optimization adds measurable value.

modules.tryIt: Build fifty preference pairs for a desired tone, run DPO on your SFT model, and have a blind judge compare outputs before and after.
modules.outcome: Use preference data when behavior is best captured as comparisons.

modules.title: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT)

topics.d: Score outputs and train toward higher scores.
Learning from rewards vs examples vs comparisons.
Code that passes tests, checkable math.
Models game the grader instead of the objective.
Usually via managed services or specialized frameworks.

modules.tryIt: Write a grader for one task, try to fool it with outputs that score well but are wrong, and fix the grader before training against it.
modules.outcome: Know when reward-based tuning is justified and write an honest grader.
modules.mentalModel: Output → grader → reward → policy update: the grader decides what gets learned.

modules.title: Distillation

topics.d: A strong teacher's outputs train a smaller student.
Filter teacher answers with evals first.
A little capability for lower cost and latency.
Inherited errors and narrow data.
Restrictions on training competing models.

modules.tryIt: Distill a large model's answers on one task into a small open model, then compare quality, latency and cost per thousand requests.
modules.outcome: Specialize a smaller model with lost capability and saved cost both measured.

modules.title: Evaluating fine-tunes

topics.d: Base model, best prompt and a stronger model.
Every candidate on identical data and scoring.
Quality, latency, cost, consistency and failure cases.
General instruction following, safety and unseen formats.
Averages can hide new failures.
Accept the result if a prompt or stronger base wins.
What improved, what regressed, and whether it is worth owning.

modules.tryIt: Run the base, prompted and tuned models through your eval suite, then add ten off-task prompts and see which model holds up.
modules.outcome: Show a fine-tune delivers value without unacceptable regressions, or that it does not.

modules.title: Serving the adapter

topics.d: Storage, loading and swapping implications.
Confirm merged weights reproduce adapter results.
Several adapters sharing one base on one GPU.
Re-run evals; quantization can erase gains.
Shared-base hosting vs your own GPU.
A common cause of poor production behavior.
Adapter, base, data and config versioned together.
Split traffic and expand while watching metrics.
Compare with the prompted baseline it replaces.
New base model, drifting inputs or new failures.

modules.tryIt: Serve two adapters on one base model, send requests to each, then swap one for a new version without restarting the server.
modules.outcome: Deploy a tuned model with versioning, rollback, measured cost and a retraining plan.
modules.mentalModel: Base model + versioned adapter + matching chat template, served behind the gateway and evaluated in production.
